about: The rule spec both local readers of a project folder follow: Eternia's (Dart, lib/core/io/project_folder_reader.dart) and hermes' (Python, agent_runtime/project_files/). Plan docs/embedded_hermes/planned/PHONE_PROJECT_FOLDERS_FILE_TREE_2026-11-21.md section 6. Each reader keeps these values as constants and a test pins them to this file; the cases in cases/*.json run on both readers.

path_grammar.rule: A request path is root-relative, '/'-separated and case-exact. It is never empty, never starts with '/', holds no '\\', no control character (U+0000-U+001F, U+007F), no empty, '.' or '..' segment, and its first segment is not a drive letter ('C:'). An absent path means the root itself.

confinement.rule: A path is resolved through every symlink before it is used; a resolved path outside the canonical root is refused 'outside_root'. While listing or searching, a symlink is listed with kind 'link' and never followed, wherever it points. A revoked grant or a stale bookmark refuses 'grant_revoked' and never falls back to a wider path.

ignore.gitignore: Only the root's .gitignore is honoured, when listing and searching (a read by explicit path is not refused for it). A line is trimmed of trailing spaces; a blank line or one starting with '#' is skipped; a line starting with '!' is not honoured (negation is a documented edge case, not worked). A trailing '/' matches directories only. A pattern holding a '/' (other than a trailing one) is anchored at the root, a leading '/' dropped; otherwise it matches an entry's name at any depth. '**/' matches any run of leading directories, a trailing '/**' everything inside, '*' any run of characters but '/', '?' one character but '/'; every other character, '[' included, is literal.
ignore.applies: The skip list and .gitignore apply to entries met while walking (tree, grep). '.git' is never listed, searched or read, by any path, through a symlink or not.

size_and_type.rule: A file whose first binary_probe_bytes hold a NUL byte is binary: listed with its size, refused 'binary' as text and skipped by grep. Text is UTF-8, decoded strictly: undecodable bytes are refused 'not_text', never replaced. A file over max_read_bytes is refused 'too_large' and skipped by grep.

patterns.rule: Neither pattern dialect is a regular expression: each is matched without backtracking over the text (row MC-FU-PROJECT-FOLDER-SEARCH-NARROWS-BY-FILE-NAME-AND-TAKES-A-PATTERN, review w1118a.84: a pattern from a remote caller runs on hermes, where a regular expression's match cannot be stopped by a deadline). Every character not named special below is itself, regular-expression characters included.
patterns.name_glob: Matched whole against an entry's name (never its folders): '*' any run of characters, none included; '?' exactly one character (code point). Holds no '/' and no '\'. 1 to max_glob code points, at most max_wildcards '*'.
patterns.line_wildcard: Matched anywhere in a line: '*' any run of characters within the line, none included; '?' is itself. Holds at least one character that is not '*', at most max_wildcards '*'; its length is the pattern's (grep.min_pattern to grep.max_pattern).
patterns.deadline: A tree with a glob or a grep that has not finished search_deadline_ms after it began is refused 'search_timeout', never answered in part: matches in the files it never reached would read as no match. The deadline is asked between entries and between lines, so no single uninterruptible step is longer than one line of one file within max_read_bytes.

arguments.path: a directory, absent for the root
arguments.glob: a file-name pattern (patterns.name_glob), absent for none: with it the entries are every file beneath path at any depth whose name matches, files only, in tree order (depth is checked but not used), and the reply carries glob

tree.reply: {path, glob?, entries, total, offset, next?}: path is the listed directory ('' for the root); entries are pre-order, each directory's children sorted by name, a file as {path, kind: 'file', size}, a directory as {path, kind: 'dir'} followed by its own entries while within depth, a symlink as {path, kind: 'link'}; at most max_entries from offset; next is present while entries remain.

read.reply: {path, size, chars, offset, content, next?}: size in bytes, chars the text's length in Unicode code points, content at most page_code_points code points from offset; next is present while text remains.

arguments.pattern: a literal string, case-sensitive; with wildcard true, a line wildcard (patterns.line_wildcard)
arguments.path: a directory, absent for the root
arguments.glob: a file-name pattern (patterns.name_glob), absent for none: only files whose name matches are searched, and the reply carries glob
arguments.wildcard: true or false, default false; when true the reply carries wildcard: true

grep.reply: {pattern, path, glob?, wildcard?, matches, total, offset, next?}: every text file under path in tree order, its lines split on '\n' with one trailing '\r' dropped; a match is {path, line (1-based), text (the line's first line_code_points code points)}; at most max_matches from offset.

status.only_on: a git root (a root holding .git); any other root refuses 'not_a_git_root'
status.reply: {path: '', entries, total, offset, next?}: every path the working tree or index holds differently from HEAD, sorted by path, each {path, state}: state 'new' for an untracked file (each listed by itself, never folded into its folder) or 'changed'; paged like tree (max_entries). Answered by the device's git: the engine's on a phone (dulwich), the git program on a desktop.

arguments.path: a file, present in HEAD or the working tree

diff.only_on: a git root; any other root refuses 'not_a_git_root'
diff.reply: {path, change, body, chars?, offset?, content?, next?}: the HEAD blob against the file, read for this one path only (never the whole tree). change is 'added', 'deleted', 'modified' or 'unchanged'; body is 'text', 'binary', 'too_large' (a side over max_read_bytes) or 'not_text'; only a text body carries the unified diff (3 lines of context, a/ and b/ prefixes, /dev/null for an absent side), paged like read. A symlink's side is its link text, never followed; a path through a symlinked folder out of the root refuses 'outside_root'.

refusals.outside_root: the path resolves outside the root (a symlink out of it)
refusals.ignored: the path is inside .git, which is never listed or read
refusals.not_a_directory: tree or grep named a file
refusals.bad_argument: depth, offset, pattern, glob or wildcard is out of bounds
refusals.grant_revoked: a granted folder's grant or bookmark no longer holds
refusals.virtual_root_read_only: a write sent to a reader of a virtual root
refusals.not_a_git_root: status or diff named a root that is not a git repository
refusals.search_timeout: a tree with a glob or a grep did not finish within patterns.search_deadline_ms
